findings.message: checkout without persist-credentials: false — tokens may leak
findings.remediation: Use persist-credentials: false when checking out external/untrusted repositories.
findings.impact: Checkout without persist-credentials: false leaves GITHUB_TOKEN in .git/config for any process to read.
findings.attack_vector: actions/checkout defaults to persist-credentials: true — token leaks via .git/config.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: README contains executable patterns with environment variable access
findings.remediation: README files should contain documentation only; executable code patterns are suspicious.
findings.impact: Executable code patterns in README files indicate social engineering or steganographic payloads.
findings.attack_vector: eval()/Function() with process.env in a README — disguised as documentation examples.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: invokes an operating-system process API (5 calls in this file)
findings.remediation: Require explicit user approval and use a fixed allowlisted command with bounded arguments.
findings.downgrade: Downgraded from high: no system-impact pattern matched near the call site.
findings.impact: Attackers can execute arbitrary OS commands on the host, leading to full system compromise.
findings.attack_vector: Plugin spawns a child process with attacker-controlled arguments; no user approval gate.
findings.risk_adjustment: Explicit risk (medium) set by caller; evidence-based risk adjustment skipped.

findings.message: invokes a file-system mutation API (5 calls in this file)
findings.remediation: Require explicit user approval and restrict mutations to an allowlisted workspace path.
findings.downgrade: Downgraded from high: no system-impact pattern matched near the call site.
findings.impact: Unbounded file-system mutations can overwrite critical files, install backdoors, or corrupt data.
findings.attack_vector: writeFile/mkdir/chmod without workspace boundary check — path is not validated against workspace root.
findings.risk_adjustment: Explicit risk (medium) set by caller; evidence-based risk adjustment skipped.

findings.message: uses eval() or new Function() to execute dynamically generated code
findings.remediation: Remove dynamic evaluation and use fixed allowlisted implementations.
findings.impact: Dynamic eval/Function allows execution of arbitrary injected code, bypassing all static defenses.
findings.attack_vector: User input or fetched data flows into eval()/new Function() without sanitization.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: downloads and pipes code directly to interpreter
findings.remediation: Do not execute code downloaded at runtime; pin and review shipped code.
findings.impact: Downloading and piping remote code to an interpreter gives attackers full RCE on the CI runner.
findings.attack_vector: curl/wget output piped to bash/node/python — no checksum verification on fetched content.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: dynamically imports code from a variable path
findings.remediation: Use static imports with allowlisted modules; avoid dynamic import() with variable arguments.
findings.impact: Dynamic import() with variable paths allows loading arbitrary modules at runtime.
findings.attack_vector: import(variablePath) — attacker controls the path to inject malicious modules.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: accesses system or user credential stores (3 occurrences in this file)
findings.remediation: Avoid direct access to credential files; use authenticated API flows instead.
findings.impact: Direct access to system credential stores allows theft of SSH keys, AWS creds, and Docker tokens.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.

findings.message: uses string concatenation or char-code construction to hide keywords (5 occurrences in this file)
findings.remediation: Use readable, explicit code patterns; avoid character-code obfuscation.
findings.impact: Character-code construction hides string literals from grep-based detection.
findings.attack_vector: String.fromCharCode() builds dangerous strings at runtime — evades static patterns.
findings.risk_adjustment: No automatic downgrade: risk changes require explicit protective controls.
